newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen flat-off $0.50-trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen flat-off $0.50-trade.

text.p: Midwest direct cash hog prices Wednesday were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt lower, with weakness expected from expanded marketings Monday and Tuesday, according to livestock dealers.
USDA interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hog marketings Monday were 117,000 head, above that day's estimate of 105,000. Tuesday's marketings were estimated at 110,000 head.

Top prices for hogs delivered to the plant in Iowa and southern Minnesota could range from $52.50-$53.50. Illinois top hog prices at the plant could range from $53.00 to $53.50 and Indiana/Ohio top plant prices could range $52.00-$53.00.
Direct cash hog prices Tuesday were $0.50 to $1.00 lower amid large marketings and an expected increase in pork supplies, market sources said.
However, declines were pared by moderately active pork movement early at mixed prices.

USDA at midday reported 52.63 loads of pork and 17.5 loads of trimmings had sold. Fresh loin prices were not fully established, butts were $2.00 per cwt higher in a light test, hams were mostly steady, bellies were not established and trimmings were steady to weak.
